  "hypothesis": "Predicted that when the boundary was at the end of character n - 1 (providing a valid versus invalid preview of the target word), readers would exhibit a preview effect on the target word across eye movement measures, including single fixation duration.",
  "design": "between/within; 2 (preview type: identical vs. dissimilar) x 2 (boundary location: character n - 1 vs. character n - 2) within-participants design",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Preview type of the two-character target word (identical vs. dissimilar preview) presented via the gaze-contingent boundary paradigm, with the boundary located after character n - 1.",
  "outcome_measure": "Single fixation duration on the target word",
  "population_and_setting": "36 undergraduate students from South China Normal University who were native readers of Chinese with normal or corrected-to-normal vision, tested individually in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 36,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Participated for course credit.",
  "analysis_plan": "Linear mixed models (LMM) for durations, including participants and items as crossed random effects, reporting regression coefficients, standard errors, t values, and p values.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants read 48 experimental sentences and 64 filler sentences using an SR Eyelink 1000 eye tracker at 1,000 Hz. One-third of sentences were followed by a true-false comprehension question."
